ENT Clinical Note – Tele-consult

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Sudden‐onset dizziness with room-spinning sensation while making breakfast this morning; no clear precipitating trigger noted.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Onset ≈ 2 hours prior to call; continuous since onset.
  • Similar but brief episode (~5–10 min) one month ago that self-resolved.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Ear: bilateral “buzzing” (tinnitus). No ear pain, discharge, or hearing loss.
  • No throat tightness/closure, voice change, dysphagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor, dyspnea, or facial/lip/tongue swelling.
  • Gait unsteady secondary to vertigo; no limb weakness.
  • No headache reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • Prior brief vertigo episode one month ago; no medical review or treatment at that time.
  • No prior ED visits, hospitalizations, or injection therapy for similar complaints.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Drug/food allergies: none reported.
  • Medications: hormone-replacement therapy for premature ovarian failure (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social context:
  • At home; husband present in household (making breakfast for him).

Objective:
- Observable findings:
  • Patient reports continuous vertigo and tinnitus; video quality limited, no visible facial asymmetry or distress noted by clinician.
- Airway/breathing: No stridor, dyspnea, or voice change reported/observed.
- Mental status: Alert, oriented; reports nausea without vomiting.
- Vitals and formal otologic/neurological examination: Not recorded.
- Accompaniment: Patient at home; no immediate chaperone in view.

Assessment:
- Probable acute peripheral vestibular disturbance (labyrinthitis vs. vestibular neuritis) presenting with 2-hour continuous vertigo and tinnitus; no red-flag neurological features presently.

Plan:
- Pharmacologic therapy:
  • Prescription sent electronically to local Lloyds Pharmacy: vestibular-suppressant/anti-vertigo medication (name not documented), 1 tablet three times daily for 10 days.
- Follow-up / further evaluation:
  • Arrange in-person appointment with clinic GP “in the next few days” for otoscopic examination, blood pressure measurement, gait/neurological assessment.
- Escalation / red-flags given to patient:
  • If develops limb weakness, sudden severe headache, or violent vomiting, proceed to Emergency Department immediately.
- Patient advice:
  • May take prescribed tablets with or without food as tolerated.
  • Contact clinic support to book follow-up appointment.
  • Remain cautious with ambulation due to unsteadiness.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements:
  – Exact name and formulation of prescribed vestibular-suppressant drug.
  – Dose/route/frequency for ongoing HRT.
  – Complete otologic, neurologic, and vital-sign examination.
  – Formal medication/allergy list confirmation, alcohol/caffeine intake, recent trauma, auditory testing, nystagmus assessment.
• Internal conflicts: None noted.
• Transcript quality: Generally clear; drug name not captured due to audio dropout.
